correctness.rationale: For each inverse merging letter the rotated inverse set can gain at most one state and only a predecessor of an existing state at a specified rotation residue. First introductions must follow the cyclic predecessor chain, spaced by at least n-1 inverse rotations. This proves #a >= (n-1)(n-2), and cardinality gives #b>=n-1. Equality forces r=0 and the unique standard word. The separate forward-subset 0-1 BFS and weighted Dijkstra checks pass for n=2..13; they supplement, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: Exact positive-weight synchronization is a natural question because generic weighted automata can have cost-ratio-dependent optimizers. The theorem determines an entire two-dimensional cost cone and a sharp all-word Parikh minimum, with an explicit inverse-gate structural mechanism. This is stronger than a routine restatement of the known shortest reset length.
